title: Market Stages Comeback on Hopes of Trade Deal
text:
Market Stages Comeback on Hopes of Trade Deal By Oct. 30, 2018 12:27 p.m. ET Order Reprints Michael Haddad Text size
Top-up Tuesday . Stocks are trending higher Tuesday after Monday’s wild ride . Earnings and updates were mixed, with General Electric ’s (GE) troubles largely expected. In today’s Intraday Update , we… …discuss a potential shift to value; …examine expectations; and …see what’s boosting Nordstrom (JWN).
Sweet Tooth
Stocks were trading up midday Tuesday, trying to regain some ground with just one more day to go in October, a month that’s lived up to its scary reputation on the Street.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average is 1.2% higher, while the S&P 500 is up 1% and the Nasdaq Composite is gaining 1.2%.
The Dow saw a 900-point swing to start the week, while all three indexes are up more than 1% today. While we may be on the more pleasant side of volatility at the moment, big moves remain. “The market evidently is repricing some assets, and this is a move that could last through the end of the year,” warns TD Ameritrade ’s JJ Kinahan . “One thing that could continue to hurt the market is negative guidance from reporting companies, as that might reinforce ideas that the economic and geopolitical outlook could be worsening.”
Yet plenty of big blue-chip stocks are still up double digits year to date, even with the recent selloffs. As Kinahan notes, some sectors were able to hold on to their gains Monday “by a sizable amount,” which could play into the idea that we’re seeing a market shift toward value, rather than a full-fledged bear market. “There’s also the economy to think about. It’s not going downhill like the stock market, at least judging from recent data,” he writes.
Ameriprise ’s David Joy echoes that idea, writing that the “ongoing search for the right level for stocks does not necessarily signal the end of the bull market,” and that valuations have been narrowed by recent selloffs to the point that they “support an argument that stocks are now fairly valued, even with somewhat reduced forward earnings expectations.”
The S&P 500 is now trading at a little over 15 times 2019 estimates, below the five-year average—although that average should be taken with a grain of salt, Joy notes, adding that what’s “reasonable going forward depends on conditions that are evolving with less than perfect clarity.”
Of course, as we’ve learned over and over in recent days, early strength can easily evaporate as the trading day draws to a close. Yet for now, at least, the rally appears to be holding its ground.
And there’s good reason for that, says LPL Financial ’s John Lynch , as he expects getting over the hurdle of upcoming midterm elections, “the solid U.S. economic backdrop, and a still-strong earnings outlook” can support stocks heading into the end of the year.
Yes, the “sugar high” of corporate tax cuts will be lapped next year, while very robust U.S. growth will come down a bit. Yet these are well-known factors, and the deceleration appears controlled. Expectations are being reset as hope for a speedy resolution to the trade-war fades. That may not be a recipe for a repeat of 2017’s stellar gains, but it’s not a reason to panic, either.
Midday Movers
Apple (AAPL) is up 0.7% to $213.67 after unveiling new gadgets .
Continental Resources (CLR) is down 1.2% to $49.76 after reporting third-quarter earnings . The energy company said it earned 90 cents a share on revenue of $1.28 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 82 cents on revenue of $1.21 billion.
Mondelez International (MDLZ) is up 2.9% to $41.28 after reporting third-quarter earnings . The snack maker earned 62 cents a share on revenue of $6.29 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 60 cents on revenue of $6.32 billion. The company expects full-year organic net revenue growth of 2%.
Nordstrom is up 5.9% to $66.25 after Wedbush upgraded the department store to Outperform .
Tesla (TSLA) is down 0.6% to $332.70, even as CEO Elon Musk disclosed another $10 million purchase of the company’s stock.
